artifacts.summary: Implementation summary for VmSwap-aware refresh memory accounting: all four plan phases completed, 18/18 matcher tests passing.

completion_data.completion_summary: Made claude-refresh.sh's memory accounting VmSwap-aware: added an overridable PROC_ROOT seam and get_vmswap_kb() helper, threaded combined RSS+swap through all three memory accumulators with a separate Swap display column, recorded the required snapshot-invariant ruling in the script header, and added six fixture-driven test cases (18/18 passing, existing cases unchanged).

memory_candidates.content: For a shell script under set -euo pipefail that needs a live /proc read alongside an existing single-atomic-snapshot race-freedom argument, the correct pattern is: (1) do the live read strictly AFTER the row's classification is fixed from the snapshot, never before or interleaved with it, so nothing downstream of the read can change which branch a row took; (2) normalize any read failure (missing line, unreadable file for an already-exited PID) to a benign default (e.g. 0) rather than propagating an error; (3) record the invariant ruling explicitly in the file's own header comment at the moment the code is introduced, arguing why the read does not reopen the snapshot's race-freedom guarantee, rather than leaving reviewers to infer it.

For shell-script-testing.md-style fixture harnesses that override an environment-seam variable (e.g. PROC_ROOT pointing at a fake /proc), combine it with a fake-ps-on-PATH subprocess harness (as already used for self-exclusion end-to-end tests) to assert on FULL script output shape rather than only the isolated helper function. This catches field-count/column mismatches between a write site (building a pipe-delimited string) and its corresponding read site (destructuring it) that a unit-level test of the helper alone would miss.
